Focus on VPC peering vs AWS PrivateLink, required regions/data residency, egress restrictions, and benchmark plan (latency/throughput). transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-14
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Alex Hartman (Redwood AE); Sofia Morales (Redwood SE); Marcus Lee (Sierra Health - Head of Platform); Aisha Khan (Sierra Health - Security Lead); Dr. Lily Chen (VP Clinical Ops); Evan Park (Infra Engineer)

[00:00] Alex Hartman: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro from our side - I'm Alex, AE, and Sofia is our SE, she'll lead the technical portion. Marcus, do you want to kick off on your side?
[00:18] Marcus Lee: Yeah, sure. Thanks Alex. We are looking to run a POC to validate private networking and data residency for clinical NLP workloads. Main asks are we need no egress from our VPC, keys managed by our KMS, and endpoints in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Timeline is tight - 2 to 4 weeks if we can get infra in place.
[00:40] Sofia Morales: Got it. We'll scope a two week benchmark window if that works. Quick clarifying q: when you say "no egress", do you mean absolutely no internet routable egress or compliant egress through a controlled NAT?
[00:55] Aisha Khan: Prefer no internet egress. All traffic must stay within our VPC or via PrivateLink. Also need SOC2 type II evidence and KMS integration for any keys. We can't have logs forwarded to third-party unless they're encrypted and stored in our account.
[01:18] Sofia Morales: Understood. Redwood Private supports VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink - both are options. VPC peering gives route-level connectivity but can be more permissive; PrivateLink gives an interface endpoint with explicit security boundaries and is often preferred by security teams.
[01:35] Marcus Lee: Any perf differences we should expect between peering and PrivateLink?
[01:44] Sofia Morales: Slightly different NAT traversal but on our infra the difference is usually negligible for inference. If you need millisecond-level latency we can benchmark both. Also note, PrivateLink imposes an extra hop but avoids route table exposure.
[02:10] Evan Park: For peering we need to ensure no overlapping CIDR and we need the exact IP ranges for your side.
[02:22] Alex Hartman: We'll provide the Redwood endpoint CIDRs and the security pack with required ports. I'll put that in the pack. (link shared: https://redwood.ai/security-pack/sierrahealth )
[02:35] Dr. Lily Chen: From a success criteria POV we care about: PII never leaving our control, end-to-end encryption, latency under ~200ms for single-turn summarization, and throughput to process ~500 tokens/sec during peak. Also accuracy: summaries must meet our clinical QA threshold (we'll provide evaluation prompts).
[03:05] Sofia Morales: That's clear. For throughput, are we talking about concurrent requests or token throughput per instance?
[03:13] Marcus Lee: Both - we have spikes of about 50 concurrent users doing chart summarization. Average prompt length is 600 tokens, average generation is 300 tokens.
[03:25] Sofia Morales: Good, that helps sizing. We'll propose a 4-GPU Dedicated pool for the POC using quantized weights to hit that throughput, and we'll provide a performance spreadsheet. We'll also run latency p99 and p50 numbers.
[03:48] Aisha Khan: On keys - do you support customer-managed keys (CMK) in their account or do keys have to be in Redwood's KMS?
[03:58] Sofia Morales: We support KMS integration. For Private deployments we can integrate with your KMS/HSM for model encryption at rest and for envelope keys. We'll document the steps in the security pack.
[04:15] Marcus Lee: Great. Region question: we need instances in us-east-1 for our US users and eu-west-1 for EU data residency. Can you host in both simultaneously for a split-residency POC?
[04:26] Alex Hartman: Yes, Redwood Private supports multi-region deployments. For the POC we recommend starting in us-east-1 and, if time permits, spin up eu-west-1. We can also route requests by policy so EU traffic stays in eu-west-1.
[04:42] Evan Park: Any dependencies on specific cloud accounts on your side? We prefer to keep redwood compute in our cloud account if possible.
[04:51] Sofia Morales: For Private we support customer-owned VPCs and cloud account installs in an on-prem or air-gapped mode. We're flexible; for this POC we can either connect to Redwood-hosted Private endpoints via PrivateLink or deploy a customer-managed control plane in your account.
[05:10] Marcus Lee: For a quick POC we probably prefer Redwood-hosted endpoints with PrivateLink into our account - less setup.
[05:19] Alex Hartman: Okay, PrivateLink it is. Next, benchmarks: Sofia, can you outline the benchmark plan?
[05:26] Sofia Morales: Sure. Plan is: 1) Baseline: run 1000 single-turn summarizations at cold start and warm start to capture startup overhead. 2) Throughput: ramp to 50 concurrent streams with batched requests, measure tokens/sec and tail latency p95/p99. 3) Network test: compare PrivateLink vs VPC peering ping/throughput. 4) Security validation: verify KMS access, no egress to internet, and audit logs sent to Sierra's account.
[05:59] Aisha Khan: For audit logs, we will only accept logs in our S3 with server-side encryption using our CMK. Does Redwood support pushing audit logs there?
[06:10] Sofia Morales: Yes, we can forward audit logs to your S3 bucket using a one-way log sink with encryption. We'll need a bucket ARN and the proper IAM role to write.
[06:24] Marcus Lee: Timeline - can we start infra provisioning this week? We need the PrivateLink service name and CIDRs.
[06:33] Alex Hartman: We'll send the PrivateLink service name and a minimal infra checklist by Monday. Realistically, provisioning and security review could take 3-5 business days on your side, then a 2-week benchmark window.
[06:50] Dr. Lily Chen: On evaluation: we'll provide a set of 100 clinical cases and expected outputs for accuracy checks. Sofia, would you run automated evals against those outputs?
[07:01] Sofia Morales: Yes - we can run the eval harness and produce a quality report with precision/recall-ish metrics for extraction tasks and ROUGE-like scores for summarization. We'll need a sanitized dataset or a reproducible prompt set.
[07:16] Evan Park: One constraint - our egress policy requires no outbound to 0.0.0.0/0 from the subnet where the interface sits. Will PrivateLink satisfy that?
[07:26] Sofia Morales: Yes. PrivateLink uses interface endpoints in your VPC that talk to the service; you can lock down the subnet and route tables so there's no internet egress. We'll validate during the network test.
[07:40] Marcus Lee: Pricing question: any POC credits or estimated costs for the Dedicated capacity for two weeks?
[07:49] Alex Hartman: We typically provide a POC discount - Sofia will follow-up with a pricing sheet. We'll also include an estimate for a 4-GPU quantized Dedicated pool for a 2-week window.
[07:59] Aisha Khan: Compliance - can you confirm SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001 and penetration testing cadence?
[08:07] Alex Hartman: Yes, SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 artifacts are in the security pack. We do quarterly Pentests; our last report is in the pack as well.
[08:18] [silence 8s - note: minor audio glitch]
[08:26] Dr. Lily Chen: One more clinical ask - model explainability. We need traceability for decisions and token-level provenance for audits. Is that supported?
[08:38] Sofia Morales: We have tracing hooks and per-request metadata that you can capture. We can include token-level logs in your audit bucket if required, subject to PII controls.
[08:51] Marcus Lee: Ok that's good. Any blockers we foresee?
[08:56] Evan Park: The main blocker is getting our security team to sign off on cross-account networking and the bucket write role.
[09:04] Alex Hartman: We'll provide a template IAM role and minimal policy to streamline that.
[09:11] Sofia Morales: For benchmarks, please prepare a representative traffic replay or list of prompts. We'll also provide a test harness repo.
[09:21] Marcus Lee: We'll share the prompt set by Friday.
[09:25] Alex Hartman: Recap then - action items: Alex to share security pack and PrivateLink details, Sofia to share benchmark plan and scripts, Sierra to provision PrivateLink and S3 with CMK, Aisha to confirm encryption/KMS, Marcus to confirm timeline. Aim to run benchmarks week of 2027-05-24.
[09:46] Aisha Khan: Sounds good. One last operational question: how do we handle model updates during the POC? If a model version changes, will it affect reproducibility?
[09:57] Sofia Morales: We'll pin a specific model version for the POC; Redwood supports version pinning and we can snapshot the model hash. If we need to patch for security, we'll notify you and can freeze updates for the test window.
[10:12] Marcus Lee: Perfect. If we get greenlight from security this week we'll proceed. Thanks everyone.
[10:20] Alex Hartman: Thanks all. I'll send the pack and pricing; Sofia will follow up with test scripts. We'll schedule the benchmark kickoff calendar invite after we get CIDRs.

End of call.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional speaker label mismatches and minor mis-transcriptions (e.g., "Redwood Privet" instead of Redwood Private). Some timestamps approximate.
